decisions.decision: How should demand data be processed?
decisions.context: The system produces forecasts weekly for each store and product. The brief does not require real-time results.
decisions.rationale: Weekly forecasts fit scheduled batches, keeping the pipeline proportionate to a three-person team (d:15, v:15.1).
consequences: Forecast freshness follows the batch schedule.
Late data may require a rerun.

decisions.decision: How should forecast results be served?
decisions.context: The system creates weekly forecasts, so consumers can use precomputed results rather than needing live model responses.
decisions.rationale: Precomputing forecasts suits the weekly reporting need and avoids operating a real-time prediction service (d:5, v:5.4).
consequences: Consumers read stored forecast outputs.
Forecasts become available after each run.

decisions.decision: How should historical inputs be reproduced?
decisions.context: Forecasts must be reproducible for any past week, which requires identifying the data used for each run.
decisions.rationale: A dedicated data version repository makes it possible to associate historical forecasts with their inputs (d:11, v:11.1).
consequences: Each run records its data version.
Storage and retention need management.

decisions.decision: How should the weekly workflow run?
decisions.context: A reliable weekly forecast requires repeatable data preparation and model building. The team also needs new ideas to reach production quickly.

alternatives.label: Scheduled data and model building pipelines

chosen.label: Scheduled data and model building pipelines

decisions.rationale: Schedule the workflow weekly and use automated data and model building pipelines to make runs repeatable while keeping experimentation connected to production (d:12, v:12.3; d:14, v:14.1; d:18, v:18.1).
consequences: Pipeline stages need maintained code and configuration.
On-demand reruns remain useful for recovery.

decisions.decision: How should training fit the workflow?
decisions.context: New model ideas need a path to production that does not disrupt the weekly forecast run. Training can remain an offline, repeatable step.
decisions.rationale: Batch training keeps model creation repeatable and aligned with the weekly workflow (d:19, v:19.1).
consequences: Training happens on a defined dataset snapshot.
Model updates wait for the next training run.

decisions.decision: What should the model building pipeline do?
decisions.context: Model experimentation should feed production through a consistent evaluation path. The pipeline can train candidates and validate them before promotion.

alternatives.label: Train, validate, and select model candidates

chosen.label: Train, validate, and select model candidates

decisions.rationale: Training, validation, and model selection give new ideas a repeatable route to production while separating candidate evaluation from the weekly forecast run (d:20, v:20.1, v:20.4, v:20.5).
consequences: Candidate runs need comparable evaluation data.
Selection criteria must be maintained.

decisions.context: The brief asks for fast delivery of model ideas without breaking the weekly run. Automated delivery of pipeline components supports iteration, with model promotion controlled by quality checks.

alternatives.label: Build, test, and deploy ML pipelines and components
Build, test, and deploy models and system components

chosen.label: Build, test, and deploy ML pipelines and components

decisions.rationale: Automating delivery of pipeline code and components shortens iteration while keeping weekly execution reproducible (d:25, v:25.2).
consequences: Releases require pipeline checks.
Promotion rules remain a separate control.

decisions.decision: What should be tested before accepting a model?
decisions.context: New models should not disrupt the production forecast run. The design space includes component tests and trained-model quality tests; these practices can be combined.

alternatives.label: Test feature logic, pipeline components, and trained model quality

chosen.label: Test feature logic, pipeline components, and trained model quality

decisions.rationale: Combine feature and pipeline unit checks with trained-model quality tests to catch failures before promotion (d:26, v:26.6, v:26.10, v:26.9).
consequences: Quality thresholds need agreement.
Tests add time to candidate evaluation.

decisions.decision: How should production model versions be managed?
decisions.context: New model ideas must reach production without breaking the established weekly run. Keeping a known previous version available supports recovery.
decisions.rationale: Retaining and redeploying the previous model provides a recovery path when a new model affects the weekly forecast run (d:10, v:10.2).
consequences: Model artifacts and metadata need retention.
Promotion and rollback need a defined procedure.

decisions.decision: How should production forecasts be monitored?
decisions.context: The weekly run must remain dependable as new models are introduced. Monitoring model performance and logging inputs and predictions can be combined.

alternatives.label: Monitor model performance and log data and predictions

chosen.label: Monitor model performance and log data and predictions

decisions.rationale: Performance monitoring plus run and prediction logs help the team assess forecast quality and investigate past runs (d:22, v:22.1, v:22.2).
consequences: Monitoring needs actual outcomes when available.
Logs need retention and access policies.

decisions.decision: How should monitoring results change models?
decisions.context: The brief prioritizes quick model iteration but also requires the weekly run not to break. Human review can gate model changes based on observed results.
decisions.rationale: Manual review keeps a person in control of model changes while the team establishes reliable monitoring and evaluation (d:24, v:24.1).
consequences: The team reviews monitoring outcomes.
Model updates may wait for review.

uncovered: Storage and retention of forecast artifacts
Feature and label definitions for store-product demand
Forecast quality metrics and promotion thresholds
Ownership and alerting for failed weekly runs
